findings.detail: Commit a gitlink update that changes module/file, leaving the child checkout clean. The parent committed bucket contains module, while the child has no changed paths because its scope uses --base HEAD. The rendered inline diff includes module/file, but simplifying that file makes changes report it in outside_scope. Directory coverage is recognized only for untracked repositories, so an edit to reviewed content is incorrectly reported as prohibited. Carry the internal paths changed by committed and staged gitlink updates into scope membership without allowing unrelated child files.
findings.evidence: collect_submodules invokes each child with --base HEAD at review-scope:328; extend_submodule_buckets expands only staged, unstaged and untracked child buckets. The committed fixture explicitly expects committed == ["module"]. render_scope uses --submodule=diff, whose installed Git documentation specifies inline content diffs. cmd_changes:1157 subtracts exact bucket paths, and lines 1158-1160 grant directory coverage only when that directory appears in untracked. Thus changed=["module/file"] produces outside_scope=["module/file"] for this committed scope.
findings.title: Parallel paths: committed submodule content is incorrectly classified as outside scope

findings.detail: The collector now includes an untracked child symlink such as module/new-link in the parent untracked bucket, but the prescribed symlink-discovery command still lists only the parent repository. It never identifies that child link. When untracked content is reviewed without intent-to-add preparation, the loop can consequently pass the path without its link-only annotation, exposing the target's contents to the reviewer. Scan the collected recursive untracked paths, or perform discovery separately in every captured repository.
findings.evidence: Both collectors prefix child untracked paths into the parent bucket at review-scope:355-358. reviewers.md:178-182 instead discovers symlinks from a single parent-level review_git ls-files --others invocation. Installed git-ls-files documentation identifies --recurse-submodules as the recursion option and supports it only for cached/stage modes, not --others. The sibling codex-aspects renderer correctly tests each flattened untracked path with -L at lines 480-489.
findings.title: Parallel paths: symlink discovery omits recursive untracked paths
